## Why we write

Field Notes started as a shared document where three colleagues kept things they found interesting. It became a blog when the document got too long to scroll.

We publish when we have something worth saying, usually once or twice a week.

articles.title: The internet's own boy
articles.description: Follow the story of Aaron Swartz, the boy who could change the world.
articles.author: david

quote.title: Aaron Swartz
quote.body: Be curious. Read widely. Try new things.

articles.body:
Aaron Swartz helped build RSS at fourteen, co-founded Reddit and spent his short life arguing that knowledge should be free to everyone.

The documentary *The Internet's Own Boy* follows him from a precocious childhood in Highland Park to the federal prosecution that ended with his death in 2013. It is not an easy film, but it is a fair one: it lets friends, family and critics speak, and it leaves the hard questions with the viewer.

Watch it with someone you can talk to afterwards.

articles.title: This shrimp is awesome
articles.description: Mantis shrimps, or stomatopods, are marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda.
articles.author: david
articles.body:
The mantis shrimp punches with the acceleration of a bullet. Its club strikes so fast that the water around it boils for a moment, producing a flash of light and a second shock wave.

It also sees the world in a way no other animal does: up to sixteen kinds of colour receptors, against our three, and the ability to detect polarised light.

None of this makes it a good aquarium pet. It can crack the glass.

articles.title: A bug is becoming a meme on the internet
articles.description: How a bug in MySQL turned into an inside joke for a generation of developers.
articles.author: sarah

quote.title: Bug #11472
quote.body: Triggers are not executed on cascading foreign key actions.

articles.body:
Some bug reports outlive the software versions they were filed against. MySQL bug #11472 was opened in 2005 and is still discussed today, mostly as a joke about how long some problems take to fix.

The bug itself is real: triggers don't fire for rows changed by cascading foreign keys. The joke is that every few years someone rediscovers it, writes a long comment, and adds their name to the list of people waiting.

If you maintain an issue tracker, there is a lesson here about closing things you will never do.

articles.title: What's inside a black hole
articles.description: Maybe the answer is in this article, or maybe not.
articles.author: sarah
articles.body:
Nobody knows, and that is the honest answer. General relativity predicts a singularity at the centre, a point of infinite density, but most physicists read that as a sign the theory has run out of road rather than a description of something real.

What we do know comes from the outside: the event horizon, the disc of gas around it and, since 2019, actual images of two of them.

The inside remains a question for a theory we don't have yet.

articles.title: Ten keyboard shortcuts we use every day
articles.description: Small habits that save a few minutes, many times a day.
articles.author: david
articles.body:
1. **Ctrl+Shift+T** reopens the tab you just closed.
2. **Ctrl+L** jumps to the address bar.
3. **Alt+Tab**, held, lets you pick a window.
4. **Win+V** opens the clipboard history.
5. **Ctrl+Backspace** deletes a whole word.

The other five are coming in the next draft.
articles.draftBody:
1. **Ctrl+Shift+T** reopens the tab you just closed.
2. **Ctrl+L** jumps to the address bar.
3. **Alt+Tab**, held, lets you pick a window.
4. **Win+V** opens the clipboard history.
5. **Ctrl+Backspace** deletes a whole word.
6. **Ctrl+W** closes the current tab.
7. **Win+Shift+S** takes a screenshot of part of the screen.

Three more to go.

articles.title: Sourdough for people who hate waiting
articles.author: priya
articles.body:
Sourdough has a reputation for being slow, and it is. But most of the time is the dough's, not yours.

Mix in the evening, fold twice before bed, shape in the morning and bake after work. Total hands-on time: about twenty minutes.

The starter is the only part that needs regular attention, and it forgives a missed feeding more often than you'd think.

articles.title: Why our office plants keep dying
articles.author: priya
articles.body:
We have killed four plants this year. A fern, two succulents and something the shop called unkillable.

The culprit, according to the nursery, is water. Everyone who walks past gives them a little, and nobody tells anyone else.

The new plan is a schedule on the fridge and a cactus.
